reason: The pinned raw, receipt, candidate, quotes, links, concept placement and Q1 check out. Q2 overstates what a returned status cannot establish and conflicts with the relevant Issuing lifecycle guide's definition of active.
required_changes: Revise the actual Q2 answer in /tmp/adyen-c65/api-explorer-balanceplatform-latest-get-networktokens-networktokenid-queries.md. Its sentence that 'a reported status cannot establish that a token was ... activated for use' would misanswer a query such as 'Does GET returning status active indicate a token that can be used for payments?' The GET raw marks status optional and lists active/inactive/suspended/closed (raw line 36), while the separate 2026-09-15 Issuing network-token lifecycle guide defines active as usable for payments (raw/adyen/docs/issuing/network-tokens/2026-09-15.md lines 63-66, 76-84). Say that a returned status reports token state, attribute any active-usability meaning to that dated guide, and keep it distinct from proof of a successful authorization, capture or settlement. Preserve the GET-only operation and snapshot boundaries.
